recipes.name: Spaghetti all'Assassina inspired by Claudia Romeo
ingredients: 24 garlic cloves, peeled and brown stem removed
2 (28 ounce) can whole passata, preferably San Marzano
instructions: For the Garlic Oil

In a small saucepan over low heat, add the oil and garlic. Cook for 45 minutes, or until the garlic is completely soft and tender. Adjust the heat throughout to ensure the garlic does not burn. This will take quite a while. - 1 cup olive oil - 24 garlic cloves peeled and brown stem removed
For the Sauce
While the garlic is cooking, add whole passata to a large saucepan over medium low heat and crush each tomato slowly with a wooden spoon. - 2 (28 ounce) can whole passata preferably San Marzano
Add salt to taste. Stir again to combine and simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring and breaking down the tomatoes occasionally. - kosher salt to taste
Transfer the cooked down passata to a large container and blend with an immersion blender until smooth. - 2 (28 ounce) can whole passata preferably San Marzano
Return to the pan and reduce on medium low for about 15 minutes - 2 (28 ounce) can whole passata preferably San Marzano
Continue to keep an eye on your garlic, it should be just about finished cooking. - For the Garlic Oil
Once the garlic has been blended, add ¼ cup garlic oil to the sauce. - ¼ cup garlic oil - For the Sauce
Then stir in the whole sprigs of basil until fragrant, remove from the sauce and set aside. - large sprig basil - For the Sauce
For the Garlic Oil Continued
Once the garlic is completely soft and tender, transfer the entire mixture to a medium kitchen container and blend with an immersion blender until almost no chunks remain. - For the Garlic Oil
Store tightly sealed in the fridge, NOT at room temperature. - For the Garlic Oil
For the Spaghetti all'Assassina
Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a small pot. Reduce to a simmer, then cover with a lid.
In a 12 inch skillet over medium high heat, add the oil and pepperoncino. Cook for 1 minute, or until the red pepper flakes are fragrant and lightly toasted. - ¼ cup garlic oil - 1 tsp pepperoncino
Then add the spaghetti and sauté, constantly stirring and flipping the pasta until each piece is golden brown. - ½ lb spaghettoni spaghetti, linguine

Next add the tomato sauce over top and stir. Pay careful attention to the consistency of the pasta until it starts to become more flexible and malleable. - 1 ½ cups sauce - ½ lb spaghettoni spaghetti, linguine
Once the pasta starts to become more malleable, add 1 cup of hot water. Bring to a simmer and reduce, turning the pasta occasionally.
Taste the pasta and ¼ cup increments of additional hot water, as needed. The pasta should not be saucy, but it should not be completely dry at this point. - 1 cup hot water as needed

Once most of the water has evaporated and the bottom of the pasta begins to burn, toss, bringing the burnt parts to the top, and continuously incorporate the noodles into the burnt sauce. - For the Spaghetti all'Assassina

Taste after another 5 minutes of cooking. The pasta should be toasted, lightly al dente, and almost caramelized. The finished dish will be dark in color and sticking to the pan in consistency. - For the Spaghetti all'Assassina
Divide onto plates and serve immediately.
